glioma.name: Glioma
glioma.description: Gliomas are primary brain tumors that originate in the glial support cells (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, or ependymal cells) of the central nervous system. They vary widely in their growth rate, infiltration pattern, and histological characteristics.
general_symptom_patterns: Persistent, worsening headaches often more pronounced upon waking
Gradual cognitive, personality, or memory changes
Focal neurological deficits such as motor weakness, numbness, or speech difficulty depending on anatomical location
associated_conditions: Neurogenetic predispositions (e.g., neurofibromatosis types 1 and 2, Li-Fraumeni syndrome)
general_lifestyle_notes: Maintain a regular sleep schedule and consistent rest periods
Implement seizure safety precautions if advised by the healthcare team (e.g., avoiding swimming alone, cooking precautions)
Coordinate with cognitive and physical rehabilitation specialists
Stay well-hydrated and follow nutritional guidance provided by licensed dietitians
glioma.disclaimer: This is not a medical diagnosis or treatment recommendation. Consult a qualified neurologist or oncologist.

meningioma.name: Meningioma
meningioma.description: Meningiomas are typically slow-growing tumors arising from the meninges—the protective membranous layers surrounding the brain and spinal cord. The vast majority are benign, though their mass effect on neighboring neural tissue can cause symptoms.
general_symptom_patterns: Gradual headaches developing over months or years
Visual disturbances such as blurred vision or visual field cutoffs if near the optic pathways
Hearing loss, tinnitus, or balance instability for skull-base meningiomas
Focal weakness, numbness, or mild sensory changes
associated_conditions: Prior therapeutic ionizing cranial radiation exposure
general_lifestyle_notes: Keep regular neuro-imaging surveillance intervals as outlined by the care team
Maintain gentle, low-impact physical exercise routines suited to balance capabilities
Adopt fall prevention strategies at home if equilibrium is affected
Engage in stress reduction practices such as guided meditation and gentle stretching
meningioma.disclaimer: This is not a medical diagnosis or treatment recommendation. Consult a qualified neurologist or oncologist.

notumor.name: No Tumor Detected
notumor.description: The MRI slice demonstrates normal neuroanatomical structures without apparent evidence of intracranial mass lesions, abnormal focal parenchymal masses, or significant midline shift within the analyzed plane.
general_symptom_patterns: If symptoms prompted the scan (such as headaches, dizziness, or sensory changes), potential non-neoplastic causes may include vascular, tension, metabolic, or cervical etiology
Absence of tumor on a single MRI slice does not eliminate non-structural or systemic neurological conditions
associated_conditions: Tension-type headaches, migraine variants, or sinus pressure
Stress, sleep deprivation, or neck strain
Benign positional vertigo or transient inner ear disturbance
general_lifestyle_notes: Maintain optimal sleep hygiene, consistent hydration, and balanced nutrition
Practice ergonomic posture during desk work and digital screen use
Keep a symptom log (trigger tracking for headaches or lightheadedness)
Follow up with your primary physician or neurologist if unexplained symptoms persist
notumor.disclaimer: This is not a medical diagnosis or treatment recommendation. Consult a qualified neurologist or oncologist.

pituitary.name: Pituitary Tumor
pituitary.description: Pituitary tumors (commonly pituitary adenomas) develop within the sella turcica at the base of the skull. Most are non-cancerous and can be secretory (hormone-producing) or non-secretory, producing symptoms through mass effect or endocrine alteration.
general_symptom_patterns: Bitemporal hemianopsia (loss of outer peripheral vision) due to compression of the optic chiasm
Endocrine-related shifts such as unexplained fatigue, temperature intolerance, or menstrual irregularities
Unexplained weight changes or sleep disruption
general_lifestyle_notes: Schedule comprehensive periodic visual field evaluations by an ophthalmologist
Monitor energy levels, hydration, and sleep consistency
Maintain open communication with an endocrinology and neurosurgical specialist team
Carry medical identification information if endocrine surveillance is ongoing
pituitary.disclaimer: This is not a medical diagnosis or treatment recommendation. Consult a qualified neurologist or oncologist.
